root_cause.text: The `drivers/counter/interrupt-cnt` IRQ handler was requested with `IRQF_NO_THREAD` even though it calls `counter_push_event()` which takes `counter->events_list_lock` as a normal `spinlock_t`, creating an invalid lock/context combination in interrupt context.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `IRQF_NO_THREAD` from `devm_request_irq()` in `interrupt_cnt_probe()`, and the CVE text shows `interrupt_cnt_isr` reaching `counter_push_event [counter]` where `_raw_spin_lock_irqsave` on `(&counter->events_list_lock)` triggered the “Invalid wait context” warning under `CONFIG_PROVE_RAW_LOCK_NESTING`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the no-thread IRQ flag so the interrupt uses standard threaded handling while preserving rising-edge triggering.
intent_record.what: The IRQ request flags passed to devm_request_irq() were changed by removing IRQF_NO_THREAD, leaving only IRQF_TRIGGER_RISING as the trigger flag.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the interrupt will now be handled using the normal threaded IRQ behavior instead of forcing a hard-IRQ-only handler path. This changes how the ISR is executed but keeps the rising-edge trigger configuration intact.

grouping_result.intent: Remove the no-thread IRQ flag so the interrupt uses standard threaded handling while preserving rising-edge triggering.

relevance_review.reason: The change removes IRQF_NO_THREAD from the interrupt-cnt IRQ request, which directly fixes the bad context/locking combination by allowing threaded handling instead of calling counter_push_event() under hard IRQ context.

candidates.rationale: This request registers the interrupt handler with IRQF_NO_THREAD on the IRQ line, meaning interrupt_cnt_isr can run in hard IRQ context even though it later calls counter_push_event() and acquires a normal spinlock, creating the invalid lock/context combination.
The IRQF_NO_THREAD flag is the direct cause of the handler being forced into non-threaded interrupt context, which is incompatible with the lock usage inside counter_push_event().

vuln_statements.explanation: This flag forces interrupt_cnt_isr to run in hard IRQ context, but the handler calls counter_push_event() which uses a normal spinlock_t (events_list_lock), creating an invalid lock/context combination.

This IRQ registration is the call site that applies IRQF_NO_THREAD to interrupt_cnt_isr; together with the flag on the next line, it makes the handler non-threaded and exposes the lock-in-IRQ-context bug.
